codeReview.summary: Solid implementation of formatTokenCount and buildFactoryUsageLines following existing Codex/Claude display patterns. formatTokenCount correctly handles null/undefined/NaN/negative/decimal inputs with manual comma formatting. buildFactoryUsageLines produces properly structured display lines: header, usage bar via printBar, per-model breakdown, billing period, and source path. Error handling (missing payload, missing usage, error response) is thorough with early returns. Zero-limit and over-limit edge cases handled correctly without division-by-zero or negative percentages. 26 well-structured tests cover all expected behaviors. Two minor non-blocking observations noted.

issues.description: The 'flags' parameter is accepted but never referenced in the function body. The --no-color behavior works via the global setNoColorFlag mechanism (in color.js), not through this parameter. The existing buildAccountUsageLines and buildClaudeUsageLines functions do not take a flags parameter. This is a minor inconsistency with the existing pattern and dead code, though it could serve as a future extension point.

The 'respects --no-color flag' test is vacuously true — buildFactoryUsageLines never produces ANSI escape codes regardless of the noColor flag (printBar uses unicode chars ████░░░░, not ANSI colors). The test passes because there are no ANSI codes to find, not because the function actively strips them. This is consistent with existing display builders (which also don't embed ANSI codes), but the test gives a false sense of coverage for the no-color feature.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The new buildFactoryUsageLines accepts a third 'flags' parameter ({noColor, ...}) that the existing buildAccountUsageLines and buildClaudeUsageLines do not accept. If future display builders should or should not accept flags, this convention should be documented to maintain consistency.

summary: Feature passes review. formatTokenCount and buildFactoryUsageLines are correctly implemented following existing display patterns with thorough test coverage (26 tests, 52 expect() calls). All required behaviors are addressed: header rendering, usage bar, per-model breakdown, billing period, source path, error handling, zero-limit, over-limit clamping, and missing-data edge cases. Two non-blocking issues noted: (1) unused 'flags' parameter is a minor deviation from existing function signatures, (2) the no-color test is vacuously true since the function never produces ANSI codes.
